_comment: Provider-unqualified exact-ID lookups through Resolve (peasant/SchemeCanonical). Each input is a real catalog model ID hosted by two or more providers; each expected records WHICH provider heads the returned slice — the representative a single-model consumer such as `bestiary show` renders — and whether the canonical-provider preference collapsed the slice to that provider alone. sole=true means the family carries a curated CanonicalProvider() that hosts this exact ID, so the preference fires and the rehosts drop out. sole=false is a fall-through control: either the family has no curated canonical, or its canonical does not host this ID, so the FULL match set is returned and the head is simply the alphabetically-first provider (the static registry is sorted by (Provider, ID)) — that value is pinned as an observed catalog fact, not as a designed guarantee.

provenance.ref: Impl-UAT report: `bestiary show claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929` rendered Provider 302ai instead of anthropic

mutation.description: family command — the curated cohere mapping. NOTE the discriminating assertion here is sole=true, not the head provider: cohere happens to sort first among this id's hosts, so the returned HEAD would read the same either way. What only the preference can produce is a slice of length 1 — without the cohere mapping the family's canonical would be empty and both hosts would come back. Every multi-provider command id cohere serves has cohere alphabetically first in the current catalog, so no stronger case exists to pin.

provenance.ref: catalog ID llama-3.3-70b-instruct, hosted by 8 providers (azure, azure-cognitive-services, cortecs, helicone, llama, llmgateway, regolo-ai, scaleway); the llama canonical is the synthetic `local` provider, which serves nothing in the built catalog, but `llama` is one of the Meta creator's curated distribution surfaces and IS present

mutation.description: the creator axis carrying a family the canonical axis cannot: Family(llama).CanonicalProvider() is `local` and never present, so before creator-first this fell through to all 8 hosts and `bestiary show` reported the alphabetically-first one (azure, a rehost) as the model's provider. Meta's own llama.com surface now wins instead. This is the creator-first-over-canonical flip the change exists for; it is measured, not incidental.
